source.text: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἰσχυρὸν καταβαίνοντα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, περιβεβλημένον νεφέλην, καὶ ἡ ἶρις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς στῦλοι πυρός, καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ βιβλαρίδιον ἠνεῳγμένον.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw another angel mighty coming down out of the heaven, having been clothed with a cloud, and the rainbow on the head of him, and the face of him as the sun, and the feet of him as pillars of fire, \v 2 and having in the hand of him a little scroll having been opened.

en.L: And I saw another mighty angel coming down from heaven, clothed with a cloud, and the rainbow [was] over his head, and his face [was] like the sun, and his feet like pillars of fire, \v 2 and he had in his hand a little scroll, opened.
en.B: Then another mighty angel came into view, coming down from heaven. A cloud was his clothing, and the rainbow crowned his head; his face shone like the sun, his legs were like pillars of fire, \v 2 and he held a small scroll, open, in his hand.
en.R: Then I saw another powerful angel coming down from heaven. He was dressed in a cloud. There was a rainbow over his head. His face was as bright as the sun. His legs were like tall columns of fire. \v 2 He was holding a small scroll in his hand. It was open.

fr.L: Et je vis un autre ange puissant descendre du ciel, vêtu d’une nuée, et l’arc-en-ciel [était] sur sa tête, et son visage [était] comme le soleil, et ses pieds comme des colonnes de feu, \v 2 et il avait dans sa main un petit rouleau ouvert.
fr.B: Puis un autre ange puissant m’apparut ; il descendait du ciel. Une nuée lui servait de vêtement, l’arc-en-ciel couronnait sa tête ; son visage brillait comme le soleil, ses jambes étaient comme des colonnes de feu, \v 2 et il tenait à la main un petit rouleau ouvert.
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai vu un autre ange puissant qui descendait du ciel. Il était habillé d’un nuage. Il y avait un arc-en-ciel au-dessus de sa tête. Son visage brillait comme le soleil. Ses jambes étaient comme de grandes colonnes de feu. \v 2 Il tenait un petit rouleau dans sa main. Le rouleau était ouvert.

es.L: Y vi otro ángel poderoso que descendía del cielo, envuelto en una nube, y el arcoíris [estaba] sobre su cabeza, y su rostro [era] como el sol, y sus pies como columnas de fuego, \v 2 y tenía en su mano un rollito abierto.
es.B: Entonces apareció otro ángel poderoso que bajaba del cielo. Una nube lo envolvía como un manto, y el arcoíris le rodeaba la cabeza; su rostro brillaba como el sol, sus piernas eran como columnas de fuego, \v 2 y tenía en la mano un pequeño rollo abierto.
es.R: Luego vi a otro ángel poderoso que bajaba del cielo. Estaba vestido con una nube. Tenía un arcoíris sobre la cabeza. Su cara brillaba como el sol. Sus piernas eran como altas columnas de fuego. \v 2 Tenía en la mano un rollo pequeño. Estaba abierto.

sw.L: Na nilimwona malaika mwingine mwenye nguvu akishuka kutoka mbinguni, amevikwa wingu, na upinde wa mvua [ulikuwa] juu ya kichwa chake, na uso wake [ulikuwa] kama jua, na miguu yake kama nguzo za moto, \v 2 naye alikuwa na gombo dogo mkononi mwake, lililofunguliwa.
sw.B: Kisha nikamwona malaika mwingine mwenye nguvu akishuka kutoka mbinguni. Alikuwa amevaa wingu kama vazi, na upinde wa mvua ulikuwa kama taji juu ya kichwa chake; uso wake uling'aa kama jua, na miguu yake ilikuwa kama nguzo za moto. \v 2 Mkononi mwake alishika gombo dogo lililokuwa wazi.
sw.R: Kisha nikamwona malaika mwingine mwenye nguvu nyingi akishuka kutoka mbinguni. Alikuwa amevaa wingu. Kulikuwa na upinde wa mvua juu ya kichwa chake. Uso wake uling'aa kama jua. Miguu yake ilikuwa kama nguzo ndefu za moto. \v 2 Alikuwa ameshika gombo dogo mkononi mwake. Gombo hilo lilikuwa wazi.

decisions.choice: a mighty angel who bears the marks of God's glory
decisions.reason: The cloud, the rainbow, the face like the sun and the fiery legs recall the throne of 4:3 and the risen Christ of 1:15-16, and some take the figure to be Christ. But John calls him "another angel", like the strong angel of 5:2, and in 10:6 he swears by God. He is most likely an angel who carries God's glory as his messenger.

decisions.choice: a little scroll, lying open
alternatives: the same scroll as in chapter 5, now opened
a different, smaller message for John to proclaim
decisions.reason: βιβλαρίδιον is a diminutive, "a little scroll". It is open, unlike the sealed scroll of 5:1, and John is to eat it and prophesy (10:9-11). Whether it is the scroll of chapter 5, now unsealed, or a separate message is not settled.

decisions.choice: feet (L); legs (B, R)
decisions.reason: πόδες can include the leg, and "pillars" fits legs better than feet.

decisions.choice: John's visions told in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("je vis") and the passé composé at Readable ("j’ai vu"); historic presents kept as presents at Literal (10:9 "il me dit", 10:11 "ils me disent")
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Revelation, and as in chapters 6-9. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: un petit rouleau
decisions.reason: The book was a scroll, as in 6:14 ("un rouleau qu’on enroule") and 5:1; "petit livre" makes readers picture a bound book.

decisions.choice: un rollito (L); un pequeño rollo (B); un rollo pequeño (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a diminutive of the word for scroll, so Spanish keeps "rollo", as in 5:1, and makes it small: the diminutive "rollito" at Literal, "pequeño rollo" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: pies (L); piernas (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word can take in the leg as well as the foot, and pillars fit legs better; Spanish follows the English steps. The same word in 10:2 is the foot set on sea and land, and there every level says "pie".

decisions.choice: gombo dogo
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a small form of the word for scroll (m2); Swahili says "gombo dogo" (a small scroll), keeping "gombo" as in chapter 5. The same in 10:9-10.

decisions.choice: miguu
decisions.reason: Swahili "miguu" covers both feet and legs, so one word gives the Literal "feet" and the Balanced and Readable "legs".

source.text: καὶ ἔθηκεν τὸν πόδα αὐτοῦ τὸν δεξιὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸν δὲ εὐώνυμον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ ὥσπερ λέων μυκᾶται.

records.literal_gloss: And he placed the foot of him the right on the sea, and the left on the land, \v 3 and he cried out with voice loud as a lion roars.

en.L: And he placed his right foot on the sea and the left on the land, \v 3 and he cried out with a loud voice, as a lion roars.
en.B: Planting his right foot on the sea and his left on the land, \v 3 he called out in a great voice, as a lion roars.
en.R: He put his right foot on the sea and his left foot on the land. \v 3 He shouted loudly, and it sounded like a lion roaring.

fr.L: Et il posa son pied droit sur la mer, et le gauche sur la terre, \v 3 et il cria d’une voix forte, comme rugit un lion.
fr.B: Posant son pied droit sur la mer et son pied gauche sur la terre, \v 3 il cria d’une voix puissante, comme rugit un lion.
fr.R: Il a posé son pied droit sur la mer et son pied gauche sur la terre. \v 3 Il a crié très fort, et on aurait dit le rugissement d’un lion.

es.L: Y puso su pie derecho sobre el mar y el izquierdo sobre la tierra, \v 3 y gritó a gran voz, como ruge un león.
es.B: Puso su pie derecho sobre el mar y el izquierdo sobre la tierra, \v 3 y gritó con voz potente, como cuando ruge un león.
es.R: Puso el pie derecho sobre el mar y el pie izquierdo sobre la tierra. \v 3 Gritó con fuerza, y su voz sonó como el rugido de un león.

sw.L: Naye akauweka mguu wake wa kulia juu ya bahari, na ule wa kushoto juu ya nchi, \v 3 naye akapaza sauti kwa sauti kubwa, kama simba anavyonguruma.
sw.B: Akiuweka mguu wake wa kulia juu ya bahari na wa kushoto juu ya nchi kavu, \v 3 akapaza sauti kwa sauti kuu, kama simba anavyonguruma.
sw.R: Aliweka mguu wake wa kulia juu ya bahari na mguu wake wa kushoto juu ya nchi kavu. \v 3 Alipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, na sauti yake ilikuwa kama ya simba anayenguruma.

decisions.choice: one foot on the sea, one on the land: a message for the whole earth
decisions.reason: Standing over sea and land, the angel claims the whole world. What he announces concerns all of it (10:6, 11).

decisions.choice: a lion's roar: the voice of the LORD in the prophets
decisions.reason: "The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken; who can but prophesy?" (Amos 3:8; compare Hosea 11:10; Joel 3:16).

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἔκραξεν, ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταὶ τὰς ἑαυτῶν φωνάς.

records.literal_gloss: And when he cried out, spoke the seven thunders the of themselves voices.

en.L: And when he cried out, the seven thunders spoke with their own voices.
en.B: When he had called out, the seven thunders spoke with their voices.
en.R: When he shouted, the seven thunders answered. They spoke with voices of their own.

fr.L: Et quand il eut crié, les sept tonnerres parlèrent de leurs propres voix.
fr.B: Quand il eut crié, les sept tonnerres firent entendre leur voix.
fr.R: Quand il a crié, les sept tonnerres ont répondu. Ils ont parlé avec leur propre voix.

es.L: Y cuando gritó, los siete truenos hablaron con sus propias voces.
es.B: Cuando terminó de gritar, los siete truenos hicieron oír sus voces.
es.R: Cuando gritó, los siete truenos le respondieron. Hablaron con sus propias voces.

sw.L: Na alipopaza sauti, zile ngurumo saba zikanena kwa sauti zao zenyewe.
sw.B: Alipokwisha kupaza sauti, zile ngurumo saba zikasema kwa sauti zao.
sw.R: Alipopiga kelele, zile ngurumo saba zikajibu. Zilisema kwa sauti zao zenyewe.

decisions.choice: seven thunders: the voice of the LORD in Psalm 29
decisions.reason: Psalm 29 describes the thunder as "the voice of the LORD" seven times. The article, "the seven thunders", suggests something known, and their words are a message from God.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, ἤμελλον γράφειν· καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ λέγουσαν· Σφράγισον ἃ ἐλάλησαν αἱ ἑπτὰ βρονταί, καὶ μὴ αὐτὰ γράψῃς.

records.literal_gloss: And when spoke the seven thunders, I was about to write; and I heard a voice out of the heaven saying: Seal what spoke the seven thunders, and not them write.

en.L: And when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write, and I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Seal up what the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write it down."
en.B: As soon as the seven thunders had spoken, I was ready to write, but a voice from heaven told me, "Seal up the words of the seven thunders; do not write them down."
en.R: When the seven thunders had spoken, I was ready to write down what they said. But I heard a voice from heaven. It said, "Keep secret what the seven thunders said. Do not write it down."

fr.L: Et quand les sept tonnerres eurent parlé, j’allais écrire ; et j’entendis une voix du ciel qui disait : « Scelle ce qu’ont dit les sept tonnerres, et ne l’écris pas. »
fr.B: Dès que les sept tonnerres eurent parlé, je m’apprêtai à écrire, mais une voix venue du ciel me dit : « Garde scellées les paroles des sept tonnerres ; ne les écris pas. »
fr.R: Quand les sept tonnerres ont parlé, je me suis préparé à écrire ce qu’ils avaient dit. Mais j’ai entendu une voix venant du ciel. Elle disait : « Garde secret ce que les sept tonnerres ont dit. Ne l’écris pas. »

es.L: Y cuando los siete truenos hablaron, yo iba a escribir; y oí una voz del cielo que decía: «Sella lo que hablaron los siete truenos, y no lo escribas».
es.B: En cuanto los siete truenos hablaron, me dispuse a escribir, pero una voz del cielo me dijo: «Guarda bajo sello lo que dijeron los siete truenos; no lo escribas».
es.R: Cuando los siete truenos hablaron, yo estaba listo para escribir lo que dijeron. Pero oí una voz del cielo. Decía: «Guarda en secreto lo que dijeron los siete truenos. No lo escribas».

sw.L: Na zile ngurumo saba zilipokwisha kunena, nilikuwa karibu kuandika; nami nikasikia sauti kutoka mbinguni ikisema, "Yatie muhuri yale ambayo zile ngurumo saba zimenena, wala usiyaandike."
sw.B: Mara zile ngurumo saba zilipokwisha kusema, nilikuwa tayari kuandika, lakini sauti kutoka mbinguni ikaniambia, "Yatie muhuri maneno ya zile ngurumo saba; usiyaandike."
sw.R: Ngurumo saba zilipokwisha kusema, nilikuwa tayari kuandika yale zilizosema. Lakini nikasikia sauti kutoka mbinguni. Ilisema, "Yafanye yale yaliyosemwa na ngurumo saba kuwa siri. Usiyaandike."

decisions.choice: seal up: keep it hidden
decisions.reason: To seal what was spoken means to keep it secret, as Daniel was told to seal up the words until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4, 9). Not everything John heard is to be made known (compare 2 Corinthians 12:4). At the end of the book he is told the opposite about his prophecy: "Do not seal up the words" (22:10).

decisions.choice: seal up (L, B); keep secret (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what sealing means here (m1).

decisions.choice: Sella (L); Guarda bajo sello (B); Guarda en secreto (R)
decisions.reason: To seal up a message is to keep it hidden, as the meaning decision says. Literal keeps "sellar", the word used for the seals through the book; Balanced says "guardar bajo sello" so the sense of keeping it closed is plain; Readable says "guardar en secreto", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: yatie muhuri (L, B); yafanye ... kuwa siri (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutia muhuri" (to seal), the same verb as for the sealing of God's servants in 7:3, here meaning to keep the words hidden (m1); Readable says "make them a secret", as the English Readable says "keep secret".

source.text: καὶ ὁ ἄγγελος, ὃν εἶδον ἑστῶτα ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἦρεν τὴν χεῖρα αὐτοῦ τὴν δεξιὰν εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ ὤμοσεν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ὃς ἔκτισεν τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ, ὅτι χρόνος οὐκέτι ἔσται·

records.literal_gloss: And the angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land lifted the hand of him the right to the heaven \v 6 and swore by the [one] living into the ages of the ages, who created the heaven and the things in it and the earth and the things in it and the sea and the things in it, that time no longer will be,

en.L: And the angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand to heaven \v 6 and swore by the one who lives for the ages of the ages, who created heaven and what is in it, and the earth and what is in it, and the sea and what is in it, that there will be no more delay.
en.B: The angel I had seen standing on sea and land lifted his right hand toward heaven \v 6 and took an oath by the one who lives forever and ever, the maker of heaven and everything in it, of the earth and everything in it, and of the sea and everything in it, that there would be no more delay.
en.R: Then the angel I saw standing on the sea and on the land raised his right hand toward heaven. \v 6 He made a promise in the name of God, who lives forever and ever. God made the sky and everything in it, the earth and everything in it, and the sea and everything in it. The angel promised that there would be no more waiting.

fr.L: Et l’ange que je vis debout sur la mer et sur la terre leva sa main droite vers le ciel \v 6 et jura par celui qui vit pour les siècles des siècles, qui a créé le ciel et ce qui s’y trouve, et la terre et ce qui s’y trouve, et la mer et ce qui s’y trouve, qu’il n’y aura plus de délai.
fr.B: L’ange que j’avais vu debout sur la mer et sur la terre leva la main droite vers le ciel \v 6 et prêta serment par celui qui vit pour toujours et à jamais, qui a fait le ciel et tout ce qu’il contient, la terre et tout ce qu’elle contient, la mer et tout ce qu’elle contient : il n’y aurait plus de délai.
fr.R: Alors l’ange que j’avais vu debout sur la mer et sur la terre a levé la main droite vers le ciel. \v 6 Il a juré au nom de Dieu, qui vit pour toujours. Dieu a fait le ciel et tout ce qu’il contient, la terre et tout ce qu’elle contient, et la mer et tout ce qu’elle contient. L’ange a juré qu’on n’attendrait plus.

es.L: Y el ángel que vi de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra levantó su mano derecha al cielo \v 6 y juró por el que vive por los siglos de los siglos, que creó el cielo y lo que hay en él, y la tierra y lo que hay en ella, y el mar y lo que hay en él, que ya no habrá más tiempo de espera.
es.B: El ángel que yo había visto de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra levantó la mano derecha hacia el cielo \v 6 y juró por el que vive por los siglos de los siglos, el que creó el cielo y todo lo que hay en él, la tierra y todo lo que hay en ella, y el mar y todo lo que hay en él, que ya no habría más demora.
es.R: Entonces el ángel que vi de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra levantó la mano derecha hacia el cielo. \v 6 Hizo un juramento en el nombre de Dios, que vive para siempre. Dios hizo el cielo y todo lo que hay en él, la tierra y todo lo que hay en ella, y el mar y todo lo que hay en él. El ángel juró que ya no habría que esperar más.

sw.L: Na yule malaika niliyemwona amesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi akainua mkono wake wa kulia kuelekea mbinguni, \v 6 akaapa kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeishi hata zama za zama, aliyeumba mbingu na vitu vilivyomo ndani yake, na dunia na vitu vilivyomo ndani yake, na bahari na vitu vilivyomo ndani yake, kwamba hakutakuwa tena na kukawia.
sw.B: Yule malaika niliyekuwa nimemwona amesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi kavu aliinua mkono wake wa kulia kuelekea mbinguni, \v 6 akaapa kwa {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} anayeishi milele na milele, Muumba wa mbingu na vyote vilivyomo, wa dunia na vyote vilivyomo, na wa bahari na vyote vilivyomo, kwamba hakutakuwa tena na kukawia.
sw.R: Kisha yule malaika niliyemwona amesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi kavu aliinua mkono wake wa kulia kuelekea mbinguni. \v 6 Aliapa kwa jina la Mungu, anayeishi milele na milele. Mungu ndiye aliyeumba anga na vyote vilivyomo, dunia na vyote vilivyomo, na bahari na vyote vilivyomo. Malaika aliapa kwamba hakutakuwa tena na kungoja.

decisions.choice: raising the hand and swearing: Daniel 12:7
decisions.reason: In Daniel 12:7 the man clothed in linen raises his hands to heaven and swears by the one who lives forever that the end will come after "a time, times and half a time". Here the angel swears that there will be no more delay.

decisions.choice: no more delay: the time of waiting is over
decisions.reason: χρόνος usually means time, and older translations read "there should be time no longer". Here, with "but in the days of the seventh angel" following, it means that God will wait no longer. It answers the martyrs' question, "How long?", and the reply that they must wait "a little while" (6:10-11).

decisions.choice: the Creator of heaven, earth and sea
decisions.reason: The oath is made by God as Creator of all three realms, as in Exodus 20:11 and Nehemiah 9:6. The angel stands on two of them and raises his hand to the third.

decisions.choice: God (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God, of whom the title is used (4:9-10).

decisions.choice: ya no habrá más tiempo de espera (L); ya no habría más demora (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek says "time will be no longer", and the meaning decision reads it as the end of waiting, not the end of time itself. Spanish "no habrá más tiempo" alone would suggest the end of time, so Literal adds "de espera" within the wording and Balanced and Readable say "demora" and "esperar".

decisions.choice: hakutakuwa tena na kukawia (L, B); kungoja (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "time will be no more" means that the waiting is over (m2), not that time itself ends; Swahili says "there will be no more delay" ("kukawia"), and Readable "no more waiting", as the English does.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ ἑβδόμου ἀγγέλου, ὅταν μέλλῃ σαλπίζειν, καὶ ἐτελέσθη τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς εὐηγγέλισεν τοὺς ἑαυτοῦ δούλους τοὺς προφήτας.

records.literal_gloss: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow trumpet, also was completed the mystery of the God, as he announced to the of himself slaves the prophets.

en.L: But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to blow his trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced [it] to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slaves the prophets.
en.B: Instead, when the days come for the seventh angel's trumpet, when he is about to blow it, God's mystery will reach its completion, the good news {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} announced to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants the prophets.
en.R: When the seventh angel is ready to blow his trumpet, God's mystery will be finished. This mystery is God's secret plan. He told it as good news to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants, the prophets.

fr.L: Mais aux jours de la voix du septième ange, quand il va sonner de la trompette, le mystère de Dieu sera accompli, comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [l’]a annoncé à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} esclaves les prophètes.
fr.B: Au contraire, quand viendront les jours où le septième ange fera entendre sa trompette, quand il sera sur le point d’en sonner, le mystère de Dieu sera accompli, selon la bonne nouvelle qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a annoncée à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs les prophètes.
fr.R: Quand le septième ange sera prêt à sonner de la trompette, le mystère de Dieu sera accompli. Ce mystère, c’est le plan secret de Dieu. Il l’a annoncé comme une bonne nouvelle à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} serviteurs, les prophètes.

es.L: sino que en los días de la voz del séptimo ángel, cuando esté a punto de tocar la trompeta, se cumplirá el misterio de Dios, como [lo] anunció a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} esclavos los profetas.
es.B: Al contrario, en los días en que el séptimo ángel haga sonar su trompeta, cuando esté a punto de tocarla, el misterio de Dios llegará a su cumplimiento: la buena noticia que anunció a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos los profetas.
es.R: Cuando el séptimo ángel esté listo para tocar su trompeta, el misterio de Dios se cumplirá. Este misterio es el plan secreto de Dios. Él se lo anunció como buena noticia a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} siervos, los profetas.

sw.L: Bali katika siku za sauti ya malaika wa saba, atakapokuwa karibu kupiga tarumbeta, siri ya Mungu itakamilika, kama alivyowatangazia watumwa {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} manabii.
sw.B: Badala yake, siku zitakapofika za tarumbeta ya malaika wa saba, atakapokuwa karibu kuipiga, siri ya Mungu itatimizwa kikamilifu, kama habari njema aliyowatangazia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} manabii.
sw.R: Malaika wa saba atakapokuwa tayari kupiga tarumbeta yake, siri ya Mungu itakamilika. Siri hiyo ni mpango wa Mungu uliokuwa umefichwa. Aliwatangazia watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, yaani manabii, kama habari njema.

decisions.choice: the mystery of God: his hidden purpose, now carried through to the end
decisions.reason: A mystery in the New Testament is God's plan, hidden before and now made known (Romans 16:25-26; Ephesians 3:3-9). Its completion is the coming of God's kingdom, announced when the seventh trumpet sounds (11:15).

decisions.choice: was completed: a past tense for something sure to happen
decisions.reason: ἐτελέσθη is a past tense used of the future: when the trumpet sounds, the mystery will be as good as finished.

decisions.choice: announced to his slaves the prophets: Amos 3:7
decisions.reason: "The Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his secret to his servants the prophets" (Amos 3:7). εὐηγγέλισεν is the verb of preaching good news: God's purpose is good news, even when it includes judgment.

decisions.choice: mystery (L, B); mystery ... God's secret plan (R)
decisions.reason: Mystery is a key term, kept at every level. Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: announced (L); the good news he announced (B); told it as good news (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out that the verb means to announce good news (m3).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: [lo] anunció (L); la buena noticia que anunció (B); se lo anunció como buena noticia (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for announcing good news; Literal keeps only "anunciar", as the English Literal does, and Balanced and Readable bring out "la buena noticia", the settled Spanish for this verb. The subject is God, left unexpressed in the verb at Literal and Balanced; at the start of a Readable sentence "Él" stands without a span, as the English "He" does.

decisions.choice: siri ya Mungu
decisions.reason: "Siri" for mystery, as in 1:20: God's hidden purpose now carried through (m1); Readable explains it as "God's plan that had been hidden", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: alivyowatangazia (L); habari njema aliyowatangazia (B); aliwatangazia ... kama habari njema (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for announcing good news; Literal keeps only "announce", Balanced and Readable spell out "habari njema" (good news), as the English does.

source.text: Καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἣν ἤκουσα ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πάλιν λαλοῦσαν μετ’ ἐμοῦ καὶ λέγουσαν· Ὕπαγε λάβε τὸ βιβλίον τὸ ἠνεῳγμένον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

records.literal_gloss: And the voice which I heard out of the heaven, again speaking with me and saying: Go, take the scroll the having been opened in the hand of the angel the standing on the sea and on the land.

en.L: And the voice that I had heard from heaven [was] again speaking with me and saying, "Go, take the scroll that is open in the hand of the angel who stands on the sea and on the land."
en.B: The voice from heaven that I had heard spoke with me once again. "Go," it said, "and take the scroll lying open in the hand of the angel who stands on sea and land."
en.R: Then the voice from heaven spoke to me again. It said, "Go and take the open scroll from the hand of the angel. He is the one standing on the sea and on the land."

fr.L: Et la voix que j’avais entendue du ciel [se mit] de nouveau à me parler et à dire : « Va, prends le rouleau qui est ouvert dans la main de l’ange qui se tient sur la mer et sur la terre. »
fr.B: La voix venue du ciel, que j’avais entendue, me parla de nouveau : « Va, dit-elle, et prends le rouleau ouvert dans la main de l’ange qui se tient sur la mer et sur la terre. »
fr.R: Ensuite, la voix venue du ciel m’a parlé de nouveau. Elle a dit : « Va prendre le rouleau ouvert dans la main de l’ange. C’est lui qui est debout sur la mer et sur la terre. »

es.L: Y la voz que yo había oído del cielo, [estaba] otra vez hablando conmigo y diciendo: «Ve, toma el rollo que está abierto en la mano del ángel que está de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra».
es.B: La voz del cielo que yo había oído volvió a hablarme. «Ve», me dijo, «y toma el rollo que está abierto en la mano del ángel que está de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra».
es.R: Luego la voz del cielo me habló otra vez. Me dijo: «Ve y toma el rollo abierto de la mano del ángel. Es el que está de pie sobre el mar y sobre la tierra».

sw.L: Na ile sauti niliyoisikia kutoka mbinguni [ilikuwa] tena ikisema nami na kusema, "Nenda, ulichukue gombo lililo wazi mkononi mwa malaika aliyesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi."
sw.B: Ile sauti kutoka mbinguni niliyokuwa nimeisikia ikasema nami tena. Ilisema, "Nenda ukalichukue gombo lililo wazi mkononi mwa malaika aliyesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi kavu."
sw.R: Kisha ile sauti kutoka mbinguni ikasema nami tena. Ilisema, "Nenda ukalichukue gombo lililo wazi kutoka mkononi mwa malaika. Yeye ndiye aliyesimama juu ya bahari na juu ya nchi kavu."

decisions.choice: a sentence without a main verb
decisions.reason: The Greek begins with "the voice" and continues with participles, "speaking" and "saying", without a main verb. The sense is plain: the voice spoke again.

decisions.choice: the scroll: the little scroll of 10:2
decisions.reason: βιβλίον is the ordinary word for scroll, but it refers to the little scroll already described.

decisions.choice: [ilikuwa] tena ikisema nami (L)
alternatives: a full sentence with a main verb
decisions.reason: The Greek sentence has no main verb (m1); Literal supplies "ilikuwa" in brackets, as the English supplies "was".

source.text: καὶ ἀπῆλθα πρὸς τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων αὐτῷ δοῦναί μοι τὸ βιβλαρίδιον.

records.literal_gloss: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little scroll.

en.L: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the little scroll.
en.B: I went over to the angel and told him to hand me the little scroll.
en.R: So I went to the angel and asked him for the small scroll.

fr.L: Et je m’en allai vers l’ange, lui disant de me donner le petit rouleau.
fr.B: J’allai vers l’ange et lui dis de me remettre le petit rouleau.
fr.R: Alors je suis allé vers l’ange et je lui ai demandé le petit rouleau.

es.L: Y fui al ángel, diciéndole que me diera el rollito.
es.B: Me acerqué al ángel y le dije que me diera el pequeño rollo.
es.R: Entonces fui adonde estaba el ángel y le pedí el rollo pequeño.

sw.L: Nami nikaenda kwa malaika, nikimwambia anipe lile gombo dogo.
sw.B: Nikamwendea malaika, nikamwambia anipe lile gombo dogo.
sw.R: Basi nikamwendea malaika, nikamwomba anipe lile gombo dogo.

decisions.choice: telling him to give: a request
decisions.reason: The infinitive after "telling" reports what John asked for.

source.text: καὶ λέγει μοι· Λάβε καὶ κατάφαγε αὐτό, καὶ πικρανεῖ σου τὴν κοιλίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῷ στόματί σου ἔσται γλυκὺ ὡς μέλι.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to me: Take and eat up it, and it will make bitter your stomach, but in the mouth of you it will be sweet as honey.

en.L: And he says to me, "Take and eat it, and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."
en.B: "Take it," he told me, "and eat it up. It will make your stomach bitter, though in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."
en.R: He said, "Take it and eat it. It will make your stomach feel bitter and sick. But in your mouth it will taste as sweet as honey."

fr.L: Et il me dit : « Prends et dévore-le, et il rendra ton ventre amer, mais dans ta bouche il sera doux comme du miel. »
fr.B: « Prends-le, me dit-il, et mange-le tout entier. Il sera amer dans ton ventre, mais dans ta bouche il sera doux comme le miel. »
fr.R: Il m’a dit : « Prends-le et mange-le. Dans ton ventre, il sera amer et te fera mal. Mais dans ta bouche, il sera aussi sucré que le miel. »

es.L: Y me dice: «Toma y cómelo, y amargará tu estómago, pero en tu boca será dulce como la miel».
es.B: «Tómalo», me dijo, «y cómetelo. Te amargará el estómago, aunque en la boca te será dulce como la miel».
es.R: Me dijo: «Tómalo y cómetelo. Te va a amargar el estómago y te sentirás mal. Pero en la boca te sabrá tan dulce como la miel».

sw.L: Naye ananiambia, "Chukua, ulile lote, nalo litalifanya tumbo lako kuwa chungu, lakini kinywani mwako litakuwa tamu kama asali."
sw.B: Akaniambia, "Lichukue ulile lote. Litalifanya tumbo lako kuwa chungu, ingawa kinywani mwako litakuwa tamu kama asali."
sw.R: Akasema, "Lichukue ulile. Litakufanya ujisikie uchungu na kichefuchefu tumboni. Lakini kinywani mwako litakuwa tamu kama asali."

decisions.choice: eating the scroll: Ezekiel's call
decisions.reason: Ezekiel was told to eat a scroll written with words of lament and woe, and it was sweet as honey in his mouth (Ezekiel 2:8-3:3; compare Jeremiah 15:16). To eat the scroll is to take God's message in fully before speaking it.

decisions.choice: sweet and bitter: God's word is good, and its message brings grief
decisions.reason: God's word is sweet (Psalm 19:11; 119:103), but the message John must now speak includes judgment and the suffering of God's people (chapter 11), and taking it in is bitter.

source.text: καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ βιβλαρίδιον ἐκ τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου καὶ κατέφαγον αὐτό, καὶ ἦν ἐν τῷ στόματί μου ὡς μέλι γλυκύ· καὶ ὅτε ἔφαγον αὐτό, ἐπικράνθη ἡ κοιλία μου.

records.literal_gloss: And I took the little scroll out of the hand of the angel and ate up it, and it was in the mouth of me as honey sweet; and when I ate it, was made bitter the stomach of me.

en.L: And I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it, and it was sweet as honey in my mouth, and when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
en.B: I took the little scroll out of the angel's hand and ate it up. It was as sweet as honey in my mouth, but when I had eaten it my stomach became bitter.
en.R: I took the small scroll from the angel's hand and ate it. It tasted as sweet as honey. But after I ate it, my stomach felt bitter and sick.

fr.L: Et je pris le petit rouleau de la main de l’ange et le dévorai, et il était dans ma bouche doux comme du miel ; et quand je l’eus mangé, mon ventre fut rendu amer.
fr.B: Je pris le petit rouleau de la main de l’ange et le mangeai tout entier. Dans ma bouche, il était doux comme le miel, mais quand je l’eus mangé, il devint amer dans mon ventre.
fr.R: J’ai pris le petit rouleau de la main de l’ange et je l’ai mangé. Il était aussi sucré que le miel. Mais après l’avoir mangé, j’ai senti de l’amertume dans mon ventre, et j’ai eu mal.

es.L: Y tomé el rollito de la mano del ángel y lo comí, y en mi boca era dulce como la miel; y cuando lo hube comido, mi estómago se amargó.
es.B: Tomé el pequeño rollo de la mano del ángel y me lo comí. En mi boca era dulce como la miel, pero cuando lo terminé de comer, se me amargó el estómago.
es.R: Tomé el rollo pequeño de la mano del ángel y me lo comí. Sabía tan dulce como la miel. Pero después de comerlo, sentí el estómago amargo y me sentí mal.

sw.L: Nami nikalichukua lile gombo dogo kutoka mkononi mwa malaika, nikalila lote, nalo lilikuwa kinywani mwangu tamu kama asali; na nilipokwisha kulila, tumbo langu likafanywa kuwa chungu.
sw.B: Nikalichukua lile gombo dogo kutoka mkononi mwa malaika, nikalila lote. Kinywani mwangu lilikuwa tamu kama asali, lakini nilipokwisha kulila, tumbo langu likawa chungu.
sw.R: Nililichukua lile gombo dogo kutoka mkononi mwa malaika, nikalila. Lilikuwa tamu kama asali. Lakini nilipokwisha kulila, nilijisikia uchungu na kichefuchefu tumboni.

decisions.choice: it happened as he was told
decisions.reason: John's action repeats the angel's words, with the order of sweet and bitter as he experienced them: first the taste, then the bitterness.

decisions.choice: dévorer for the compound verb, manger for the simple one (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a strengthened verb, "eat up", and then the plain verb; Literal shows the difference with "dévorer" and "manger", as in 10:9. Balanced says "manger tout entier"; Readable just "manger".

source.text: Καὶ λέγουσίν μοι· Δεῖ σε πάλιν προφητεῦσαι ἐπὶ λαοῖς καὶ ἔθνεσιν καὶ γλώσσαις καὶ βασιλεῦσιν πολλοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And they say to me: It is necessary you again to prophesy about peoples and nations and tongues and kings many.

en.L: And they say to me, "You must prophesy again about many peoples and nations and languages and kings."
en.B: Then they said to me, "Once more you must prophesy, concerning many peoples and nations and languages and kings."
en.R: Then I was told, "You must speak God's message again. You must tell it about many peoples, nations, languages, and kings."

fr.L: Et ils me disent : « Il faut que tu prophétises de nouveau sur beaucoup de peuples, et de nations, et de langues, et de rois. »
fr.B: Puis on me dit : « Il faut que tu prophétises encore, au sujet de nombreux peuples, nations, langues et rois. »
fr.R: Ensuite, on m’a dit : « Tu dois encore annoncer le message de Dieu. Tu dois l’annoncer au sujet de beaucoup de peuples, de nations, de langues et de rois. »

es.L: Y me dicen: «Es necesario que profetices otra vez acerca de muchos pueblos y naciones y lenguas y reyes».
es.B: Entonces me dijeron: «Tienes que profetizar otra vez acerca de muchos pueblos, naciones, lenguas y reyes».
es.R: Luego me dijeron: «Tienes que anunciar otra vez el mensaje de Dios. Tienes que anunciarlo acerca de muchos pueblos, naciones, lenguas y reyes».

sw.L: Na wananiambia, "Imekupasa kutoa unabii tena juu ya watu na mataifa na lugha na wafalme wengi."
sw.B: Kisha nikaambiwa, "Ni lazima utoe unabii tena kuhusu jamii nyingi, mataifa, lugha na wafalme."
sw.R: Kisha nikaambiwa, "Ni lazima useme tena ujumbe wa Mungu. Utauhubiri kuhusu jamii nyingi, mataifa, lugha na wafalme."

decisions.choice: they say: I was told
decisions.reason: The plural with no subject is a way of saying that someone spoke without naming who.

decisions.choice: about, or against, many peoples
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ can mean "about", "to" or "against". The prophecy concerns the nations and their kings, and much of it is judgment. Jeremiah was appointed "over nations and over kingdoms" (Jeremiah 1:10).

decisions.choice: kings in place of tribes
decisions.reason: The familiar list, "peoples, nations, languages, tribes" (5:9; 7:9), here ends with "many kings": the prophecy that follows deals with rulers and powers (chapters 13 and 17).

decisions.choice: prophesy (L, B); speak God's message (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what it means to prophesy.

decisions.choice: on me dit (B); on m’a dit (R)
decisions.reason: The plural "they say" names no one (m1); French says this with the impersonal "on", which keeps the active voice where English Readable has "I was told". Literal keeps "ils me disent".

decisions.choice: profetices (L); profetizar (B); anunciar el mensaje de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: "Profetizar" is the plain Spanish word for speaking as a prophet; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. The impersonal "they say" is kept as "me dicen" at Literal and "me dijeron" at Balanced and Readable, which Spanish uses for "I was told".

decisions.choice: kutoa unabii (L, B); kusema ujumbe wa Mungu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutoa unabii" is to speak as a prophet (m2); "kutabiri" suggests foretelling only. Readable says "speak God's message", as the English Readable does.
